Knowing Python syntax is different from being effective with Python.

For Data Science, the next layer is:

```text
Python
 ├── NumPy       → numerical arrays
 ├── pandas      → tabular data
 ├── visualization
 ├── scikit-learn → ML workflows
 └── algorithms  → computational thinking
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Key ideas
`array` `shape` `axis` `vectorization` `DataFrame` `index`
`groupby` `merge` `complexity` `stack` `queue` `hash map`
`tree` `graph` `recursion`
:::

## Data Science Python

Start with arrays before treating pandas as magic.

**NumPy Quickstart:**  
https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/quickstart.html

**pandas Getting Started:**  
https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/getting_started/

**10 Minutes to pandas:**  
https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/user_guide/10min.html

**scikit-learn Getting Started:**  
https://scikit-learn.org/stable/getting_started.html

A useful translation:

```text
Python list       → general collection
NumPy ndarray     → numerical computation
pandas DataFrame  → labeled tabular analysis
Spark DataFrame   → distributed tabular computation
```

## Algorithms & data structures

Learn the concepts before memorizing interview templates:

```text
Big-O
arrays / strings
hash maps / sets
stacks / queues
linked lists
binary search
sorting
trees
heaps
graphs
recursion
dynamic programming
```

### Resources

- **Python Data Structures tutorial:** https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/datastructures.html
- **VisuAlgo:** https://visualgo.net/en — visual intuition for algorithms/data structures.
- **LeetCode:** https://leetcode.com/ — extensive coding-problem practice.
- **HackerRank:** https://www.hackerrank.com/ — structured programming/problem-solving practice.

## Interview preparation

Use problems as **reasoning practice**, not a memorization contest.

```text
1. Restate problem
2. Work a tiny example
3. Describe brute force
4. Identify data structure
5. Improve complexity
6. Code
7. Test edge cases
8. State time + space complexity
```

For DS interviews, also practice writing ordinary Python transformations without relying on pandas for everything.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Common trap
Solving 300 problems badly is less useful than solving 60 problems while understanding **why the algorithm works, its invariants, complexity and alternatives**.
:::

## Recommended route

**Python fundamentals → NumPy → pandas → 30–50 core algorithm problems → role-specific interview problems**

Keep this page as a map; use the linked resources as the classroom.
